criteria.reasoning: The report calls her "a novelist and philanthropist" and says "She married Jeff Bezos in 1993, and they divorced in 2019." It adds that she "holds no Amazon position today." The identification is correct.

The report says "In the 2019 divorce settlement she received 25% of the couple's Amazon stock: about 19.7 million shares, roughly 4% of the company", which matches the record. It gives a dated net-worth figure: "Bloomberg put her at about $42.7 billion on April 18, 2026."

The report states "Latest disclosed holding: 139,132,131 Amazon shares as of September 30, 2024, about 1.3% of the company." That figure is superseded by the 81.1 million shares as of 2025-09-30, yet it is presented as the latest holding.

The report gives "Cumulative: $19.25 billion in more than 2,450 gifts since 2019" as its cumulative total. That is the superseded December 2024 figure, presented as current, and the report gives no ~$26 billion total.

The report says "A small internal team and a large network of advisors do 'quiet research'... The team then contacts the organizations it has selected. She does not accept applications or unsolicited proposals." That explains both the policy and how recipients are chosen.
The engagement strategy recommends "Invite Ms. Scott to our spring Celebration of Learning breakfast as an honored guest." Inviting her to an event is an explicit fail condition.

The open call is described as launched in March 2023, giving "$640 million to 361 organizations" in March 2024, and "It is completed, and no open call is accepting applications." Watching for a future call is allowed.
Under "Unrestricted, no strings", the report says gifts are made "for use however they choose" and that grantees are not required to report. Her gifts are clearly described as unrestricted.

The Atlanta table credits Morehouse College with "$20 million; $38 million (unrestricted) | July 2020; Nov. 2025", and Section 7 cites "the Spelman, Clark Atlanta and Morehouse gifts of November 2025." Morehouse received no direct gift after 2020, so this is an explicit fail condition.

The report names Achieve Atlanta $8 million, Southern Education Foundation $6 million, Communities In Schools of Atlanta $4 million and GEEARS $3 million, all correct. KIPP Metro Atlanta and Sheltering Arms are listed with "amounts not disclosed".
The report states "In 2021 she married Dan Jewett, a Seattle science teacher, and they live in Seattle." It never mentions the divorce. The present tense describes her as currently married to Jewett.

Under "Be findable and fundable" the strategy lists stable finances, a multi-year track record, measurement and evidence of outcomes, and experienced leadership representative of the community. That covers all four published indicators.

The report contradicts the fact sheet on several points. It credits Morehouse with a $38 million November 2025 gift, which the sheet says it did not receive. It presents 139.1 million shares as the latest holding and $19.25 billion as cumulative giving, both superseded. It also describes her as living with Dan Jewett when the sheet says she is not married.
